title: Roll and Race
story: Keepers roll supplies through a gate to a teammate, then both race to new jobs.
setup: Make pairs 8 to 12 yards apart with a two-cone gate between them. Give every pair a ball and leave safe space between channels.
instructions: One player begins as goalkeeper with the ball in hands and rolls it through the gate.
The teammate receives, dribbles around an outside cone and returns to the goalkeeper spot.
The roller follows to the receiving spot, so roles change every turn.
Let each pair choose a wider gate or longer channel when ready.
coach_lens: Notice a low, accurate roll into the receiver's path, a ready receiving shape and both players moving immediately after release.
questions: Where would your teammate like the ball?
How can you make the roll easy to receive?

simplify: Widen the gate and shorten the channel.
challenge: Place two gates so the goalkeeper scans and chooses one.
low_attendance: Keep pairs; the coach can join an unmatched player.
high_attendance: Add channels so every pair has a ball.
limited_equipment: Use a field line as the target and one shared outside marker per two channels.

safety: Roll underarm along the ground; do not punt or throw toward another group.
Use only stationary goalkeeper handling in this introductory activity.

diagram.alt: Pairs work in separate channels; a goalkeeper rolls through a central gate and the receiver dribbles around an outside cone as roles rotate.

source.title: MiniRoos Program Leader Session Guide 7-9
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored rotating distribution activity applying Football Australia principles of maximum involvement, short explanations, safe ground play and small groups. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
